reader.requirement: At 85 the POINTER item (any usage, elementary integer, no P) is the program's responsibility to set above zero; its value is taken as the first receiving position, and a value below one or beyond the receiver is handled by GR9 (overflow, no transfer, pointer unchanged), never by any other action.
reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior over StringEmitter.cs and CobolStringOps.cs: none; StrUnstrIsInteger in BindString has no edition test.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f14_01 covers P = 1, 3, 5 and 0; not exercised: a negative signed pointer, a binary pointer, the largest pointer, a subscripted pointer

probes.expected: pointer = size moves one char then overflows; size+1, negative and 18-digit pointers overflow with no transfer and keep their value; COMP pointer advances; subscripted pointer PT(I) advances

probes.printed: COBOL1651 for a scaled operand (the same StrUnstrIsInteger screen guards identifier-4 per SR5)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.25.4 GR5  (║6.25.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR5
OK  §1985:VI.6.25.4 GR9  (║6.25.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR9

reader.notes: GR5 is a user obligation; the compiler reads the pointer by value (saturating HostInt64), checks it before each move in StringTransfer, and stores it back only when it moved, so a violated precondition yields the GR9 behaviour.

refuter.evidence: cite.py 'OK §1985:VI.6.25.4 GR5 the text is in GR5' (a user obligation). subp.cob: POINTER that is also the subscript of a sender and of a delimiter is read once at start and advanced only by moves ('1 ... 05', '2 ... 02'); pointer 3 into X(8) with 7 chars stops at 9 with overflow, pointer not otherwise changed. Reader's below-one/beyond-size probes stand; GR5 imposes nothing beyond GR9's behaviour on the implementation.
